name: What if my bathroom expansion makes the room feel darker?

mainEntity.name: Why does a bigger bathroom sometimes end up feeling darker, and how do I avoid that?
mainEntity.text: Why does a bigger bathroom sometimes end up feeling darker, and how do I avoid that?

acceptedAnswer.text: A larger bathroom can still feel dark if the new layout blocks windows, adds heavy partitions, or uses too many matte and low-reflective surfaces. That is why lighting design matters as much as square footage. Glass shower enclosures, light-colored tile, reflective finishes, and well-placed mirrors can make the expanded room feel brighter and more open. Layered lighting is important too, including ambient lighting, task lighting at the vanity, and good shower illumination. If natural light exists, the design should protect it rather than bury it behind a wall or oversized cabinet. In some cases, a bathroom expansion can actually improve brightness if the old layout was cramped and obstructed. The key is to balance privacy, storage, and openness. A well-designed expansion should feel airy, not cave-like, even if the room is larger on paper.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bathroom can feel darker after expansion if walls, partitions, or fixtures block natural light. Using glass, brighter finishes, layered lighting, and better mirror placement usually prevents the room from feeling smaller or dimmer.
